Module 20
HTML Forms & HTTP in Django

Module 20 — HTML Forms & HTTP in Django

We are now starting Unit IV — Forms.

Before learning Django's built-in Form class, you need to understand HTML forms and how browsers send data to Django.

This is extremely important because later:

text
HTML Form
   ↓
HTTP GET/POST
   ↓
Django View
   ↓
request.GET / request.POST
   ↓
Validation
   ↓
Database

will become the foundation of login forms, registration, CRUD applications, search forms, etc.

1. What Is a Form?

A form is an HTML mechanism used to collect information from a user.

Examples:

  • Login
  • Registration
  • Search
  • Contact form
  • Student registration
  • Product creation
  • Feedback

A simple form:

html
<form>
    <input type="text">
    <button type="submit">Submit</button>
</form>

The user enters information and submits it.

2. Basic HTML Form Structure

The general syntax is:

html
<form method="POST" action="/students/">

    <input type="text" name="name">

    <button type="submit">
        Submit
    </button>

</form>

There are three important concepts here:

text
form
 ├── method
 ├── action
 └── form fields

3. The method Attribute

The method determines how the browser sends the form data.

Most commonly:

html
method="GET"

or:

html
method="POST"

Example:

html
<form method="GET">

or:

html
<form method="POST">

4. The action Attribute

action specifies where the form data should be sent.

Example:

html
<form action="/students/" method="POST">

This means:

When submitted, send the form data to /students/.

You can also use Django URL reversing:

html
<form action="{% url 'students' %}" method="POST">

This is generally preferable to hardcoding URLs.

5. What Is <input>?

input creates a field where users can enter/select data.

Example:

html
<input type="text" name="name">

Common input types:

text
text
password
email
number
date
checkbox
radio
file
submit

6. The name Attribute ⭐

This is very important.

Consider:

html
<input type="text" name="username">

The:

text
name="username"

becomes the key that Django receives.

If the user enters:

text
Aman

Django can access:

python
request.POST.get("username")

So:

text
HTML
 ↓
name="username"
 ↓
request.POST["username"]

7. id vs name

Beginners often confuse these.

Example:

html
<input
    type="text"
    id="username"
    name="username"
>

id

Primarily identifies the HTML element in the page and is commonly used by:

  • CSS
  • JavaScript
  • <label for="...">

name

Identifies the form field when form data is submitted.

For Django form processing, name is crucial.

8. <label>

A label describes a form field.

html
<label for="username">
    Username:
</label>

<input
    type="text"
    id="username"
    name="username"
>

The:

html
for="username"

matches:

html
id="username"

9. Complete GET Form

Let's create a search form.

html
<form method="GET">

    <label for="query">
        Search:
    </label>

    <input
        type="text"
        id="query"
        name="query"
    >

    <button type="submit">
        Search
    </button>

</form>

Suppose the user enters:

text
Django

The browser may navigate to:

text
/search/?query=Django

The data appears in the URL.

10. Why Does GET Put Data in the URL?

GET requests commonly use the query string.

For example:

text
/search/?query=Django

Break it down:

text
/search/
   ↓
path

?
   ↓
start of query string

query=Django
   ↓
key=value

11. Multiple GET Parameters

Suppose:

html
<input type="text" name="name">

<input type="number" name="age">

User enters:

text
name = Aman
age = 21

The URL can become:

text
/search/?name=Aman&age=21

& separates parameters.

12. Receiving GET Data in Django

View:

python
from django.http import HttpResponse

def search(request):

    query = request.GET.get("query")

    return HttpResponse(
        f"You searched for: {query}"
    )

Suppose the browser requests:

text
/search/?query=Django

Then:

python
request.GET.get("query")

returns:

text
Django

13. Why Use .get()?

You learned this earlier.

Instead of:

python
query = request.GET["query"]

prefer:

python
query = request.GET.get("query")

when the parameter may be missing.

If missing:

python
request.GET.get("query")

normally returns:

python
None

while direct indexing can raise a KeyError.

You can also provide a default:

python
query = request.GET.get(
    "query",
    ""
)

14. GET Form Flow

Understand this completely:

text
User enters Django
       ↓
Clicks Search
       ↓
Browser creates GET request
       ↓
/search/?query=Django
       ↓
Django URL routing
       ↓
search(request)
       ↓
request.GET
       ↓
query = "Django"
       ↓
Response

15. POST Form

Now:

html
<form method="POST">

POST sends the form data in the HTTP request body rather than putting ordinary form fields into the URL query string.

Example:

html
<form method="POST">

    <input
        type="text"
        name="username"
    >

    <input
        type="password"
        name="password"
    >

    <button type="submit">
        Login
    </button>

</form>

16. Receiving POST Data

Django provides:

python
request.POST

Example:

python
def login(request):

    username = request.POST.get("username")
    password = request.POST.get("password")

    return HttpResponse(
        f"Username: {username}"
    )

17. GET vs POST

This is a must-know viva question.

GET POST
Commonly used to retrieve/search data Commonly used to submit/change data
Data commonly appears in URL query string Form data is sent in request body
Can be bookmarked/shared as a URL Usually not represented by the form data in the URL
Suitable for search/filtering Suitable for create/update/login operations
Should not be relied on for sensitive data Better suited for sensitive/state-changing submissions
Parameters commonly accessed via request.GET Parameters commonly accessed via request.POST

18. Important Security Point

A common misconception is:

"POST is automatically secure."

False.

POST does not encrypt data.

If you need confidentiality in transit, use:

text
HTTPS

So:

text
POST + HTTP

is not automatically secure.

Whereas:

text
POST + HTTPS

encrypts the network connection.

19. GET Is Usually Used for Retrieval

Examples:

text
Search
Filter
Sort
Pagination
Viewing resources

Example:

text
/products/?category=laptops

The request is asking:

Give me products matching this criterion.

20. POST Is Usually Used for State Changes

Examples:

text
Create student
Submit feedback
Register user
Login
Create order
Update data through a form

The key idea is:

GET is generally safe/read-oriented; POST is generally used when submitting data that can cause a state change.

21. Important: HTML Form Needs name

Consider:

html
<input
    type="text"
    id="username"
>

There is no:

text
name="username"

When submitted, Django won't receive a normal form field under "username".

Correct:

html
<input
    type="text"
    id="username"
    name="username"
>

22. Submit Button

You can write:

html
<button type="submit">
    Submit
</button>

or:

html
<input type="submit" value="Submit">

Both can submit a form.

23. Text Input

html
<input
    type="text"
    name="name"
>

24. Email Input

html
<input
    type="email"
    name="email"
>

The browser may perform basic client-side validation.

But never rely only on browser validation.

Server-side validation is still required.

We'll cover this in depth later.

25. Password Input

html
<input
    type="password"
    name="password"
>

The browser visually masks the entered characters.

But again:

type="password" does not encrypt network traffic.

Use HTTPS.

26. Number Input

html
<input
    type="number"
    name="age"
>

The browser can provide numeric input controls.

But Django still receives form values through the request and validation/conversion must be handled appropriately.

27. Date Input

html
<input
    type="date"
    name="dob"
>

28. Textarea

For larger text:

html
<textarea
    name="message"
></textarea>

Example:

html
<label for="message">
    Message:
</label>

<textarea
    id="message"
    name="message"
    rows="5"
    cols="30"
></textarea>

29. Select Dropdown

html
<select name="course">

    <option value="cse">
        Computer Science
    </option>

    <option value="it">
        Information Technology
    </option>

</select>

If the user chooses Computer Science, Django receives:

text
course=cse

not necessarily:

text
course=Computer Science

because the submitted value comes from the value attribute.

30. Checkbox

html
<input
    type="checkbox"
    name="agree"
    value="yes"
>

If checked, the browser submits the field.

If unchecked, the field is generally absent from the submitted form data.

So:

python
agree = request.POST.get("agree")

might return:

text
yes

when checked and None when absent.

31. Radio Buttons

Example:

html
<input
    type="radio"
    name="gender"
    value="male"
>

<input
    type="radio"
    name="gender"
    value="female"
>

Both use the same:

text
name="gender"

but different values.

Only the selected option is submitted.

32. Complete Student Form

Let's build a manual HTML form.

html
<form method="POST">

    <label for="name">
        Name:
    </label>

    <input
        type="text"
        id="name"
        name="name"
    >

    <br><br>

    <label for="age">
        Age:
    </label>

    <input
        type="number"
        id="age"
        name="age"
    >

    <br><br>

    <label for="course">
        Course:
    </label>

    <select
        id="course"
        name="course"
    >

        <option value="cse">
            Computer Science
        </option>

        <option value="it">
            Information Technology
        </option>

    </select>

    <br><br>

    <button type="submit">
        Submit
    </button>

</form>

33. Processing the Form

View:

python
from django.http import HttpResponse

def student_create(request):

    if request.method == "POST":

        name = request.POST.get("name")
        age = request.POST.get("age")
        course = request.POST.get("course")

        return HttpResponse(
            f"Name: {name}, Age: {age}, Course: {course}"
        )

    return render(
        request,
        "student_form.html"
    )

Notice:

python
if request.method == "POST":

We only process submitted data when the request is POST.

34. GET and POST in the Same View

This pattern is extremely common.

python
def student_create(request):

    if request.method == "POST":

        name = request.POST.get("name")

        return HttpResponse(
            f"Student: {name}"
        )

    return render(
        request,
        "student_form.html"
    )

Meaning:

text
GET
 ↓
Display form

POST
 ↓
Process submitted form

35. Why Is This Pattern Useful?

When the user first opens:

text
/students/create/

the browser sends:

text
GET

Django displays the form.

After clicking Submit:

text
POST

Django processes the submitted data.

So one URL can handle both stages.

36. Form With action

You can explicitly specify:

html
<form
    action="{% url 'student_create' %}"
    method="POST"
>

This is usually better than:

html
<form action="/students/create/" method="POST">

because URL names make templates less dependent on hardcoded paths.

37. The action Can Be Empty

You may also see:

html
<form method="POST">

This submits to the current URL.

For example, if you're on:

text
/students/create/

the form submits to that URL unless another action is specified.

38. GET Form With Search

Let's build a complete search page.

Template:

html
<form method="GET">

    <input
        type="text"
        name="query"
        placeholder="Search students"
    >

    <button type="submit">
        Search
    </button>

</form>

View:

python
def search(request):

    query = request.GET.get(
        "query",
        ""
    )

    return render(
        request,
        "search.html",
        {
            "query": query
        }
    )

Template:

html
{% if query %}

    <p>You searched for: {{ query }}</p>

{% endif %}

39. POST Form With Data

Template:

html
<form method="POST">

    <input
        type="text"
        name="name"
    >

    <button type="submit">
        Submit
    </button>

</form>

View:

python
def student(request):

    if request.method == "POST":

        name = request.POST.get("name")

        return HttpResponse(
            f"Student name: {name}"
        )

    return render(
        request,
        "student.html"
    )

40. One Important Problem

Our POST form currently lacks:

html
{% csrf_token %}

In Django, POST forms should normally include CSRF protection.

So a proper Django POST form is:

html
<form method="POST">

    {% csrf_token %}

    <input
        type="text"
        name="name"
    >

    <button type="submit">
        Submit
    </button>

</form>

Don't worry about the detailed mechanics yet.

CSRF is the next important Forms topic, and we'll study it properly in Module 23.

41. Why Does Django Require CSRF?

CSRF stands for:

Cross-Site Request Forgery

It's a security attack where a malicious site attempts to cause a user's browser to send an unwanted request to a site where the user is authenticated.

Django provides CSRF protection for state-changing requests such as POST.

We'll go deeply into:

text
CSRF token
middleware
{% csrf_token %}
403 errors
CSRF_COOKIE

later.

42. GET Does Not Usually Need CSRF Token

You normally don't write:

html
<form method="GET">
    {% csrf_token %}

for a normal GET form.

CSRF protection is primarily relevant to unsafe/state-changing HTTP methods such as POST.

43. Important Form Flow

For a POST form:

text
Browser
   │
   │ GET /students/create/
   ▼
Django View
   │
   ▼
Render Form
   │
   ▼
Browser
   │
   │ User fills form
   │
   │ POST /students/create/
   ▼
Django
   │
   ├── CSRF check
   │
   ├── Read request.POST
   │
   ├── Validate data
   │
   └── Process data

This is the foundation for everything we'll do with Django Forms.

44. Client-Side vs Server-Side Validation

Suppose:

html
<input
    type="email"
    name="email"
    required
>

The browser can check some conditions.

That's client-side validation.

But a malicious user can bypass browser checks.

Therefore Django must perform:

Server-side validation

Never trust client-side validation alone.

45. required

HTML:

html
<input
    type="text"
    name="name"
    required
>

The browser can prevent normal submission if the field is empty.

But Django should still validate the submitted value.

46. Why Django Forms Exist

At this point you might think:

"Why don't we just create HTML forms manually?"

We can.

But large applications quickly become difficult.

Suppose you have:

text
Name
Email
Age
Password
Phone
Date of birth
Address
Course

You need to manage:

  • HTML generation
  • validation
  • error messages
  • cleaning data
  • security
  • redisplaying invalid input
  • field types
  • widgets

Django's Forms framework helps manage these tasks.

That's what we'll learn next.

47. HTML Forms vs Django Forms

HTML Form

You manually write:

html
<input type="text" name="name">

and manually process:

python
request.POST.get("name")

Django Form

You define fields in Python:

python
class StudentForm(forms.Form):

    name = forms.CharField()
    age = forms.IntegerField()

Django can then help with:

  • rendering
  • validation
  • cleaned data
  • errors

48. Important Distinction

Don't confuse:

text
HTML Form

with:

text
Django Form

HTML forms are a browser/web standard.

Django Forms are a Python framework provided by Django to make form handling easier and safer.

49. Common Mistakes

Mistake 1 — Forgetting name

Wrong:

html
<input type="text" id="name">

Correct:

html
<input
    type="text"
    id="name"
    name="name"
>

Mistake 2 — Reading POST data from request.GET

Wrong:

python
name = request.GET.get("name")

for a POST submission.

Correct:

python
name = request.POST.get("name")

Mistake 3 — Reading GET data from request.POST

Wrong:

python
query = request.POST.get("query")

for a GET search form.

Correct:

python
query = request.GET.get("query")

Mistake 4 — Forgetting CSRF

For a normal Django POST form:

html
<form method="POST">
    {% csrf_token %}

Mistake 5 — Thinking POST Encrypts Data

It doesn't.

Use HTTPS for encryption in transit.

Mistake 6 — Trusting Browser Validation

HTML validation can be bypassed.

Always validate on the server.

Q1. What is an HTML form?

An HTML form is a mechanism for collecting user input and submitting it to a server.

Q2. What are the common HTTP methods used with forms?

GET and POST.

It specifies the HTTP method used when submitting the form.

In the URL query string.

text

52. Viva — POST

Answer:

53. Viva — GET vs POST

Teacher:

Which one should you use for login?

Answer:

POST should generally be used because login is a form submission involving credentials and represents a stateful/authentication operation. HTTPS must also be used because POST itself does not encrypt data.

54. Viva — request.POST

Teacher:

What is request.POST?

Answer:

request.POST is a Django QueryDict containing form data submitted using POST.

55. Viva — request.GET

Teacher:

What is request.GET?

Answer:

request.GET is a Django QueryDict containing query parameters submitted through the URL, commonly by GET requests.

56. Viva — name vs id

Teacher:

Why is name important in a form?

Answer:

The name attribute identifies the field in the submitted form data, while id primarily identifies the HTML element for the document, CSS, JavaScript, and labels.

Module 21
Django Forms

Module 21 — Django Forms

Now we move from manual HTML forms to Django's built-in Forms framework.

This is a very important module because Django Forms combine:

text
HTML generation
+
Input handling
+
Validation
+
Error handling
+
Cleaned data

into a structured Python class.

1. Why Django Forms?

Previously, we created a form manually:

html
<form method="POST">

    {% csrf_token %}

    <input type="text" name="name">

    <input type="email" name="email">

    <button type="submit">
        Submit
    </button>

</form>

Then manually processed:

python
name = request.POST.get("name")
email = request.POST.get("email")

For a small form, that's okay.

But imagine 20 fields.

You would need to manually handle:

  • HTML fields
  • validation
  • required fields
  • error messages
  • type conversion
  • redisplaying values
  • security
  • invalid input

Django Forms simplify this.

2. What Is a Django Form?

A Django Form is a Python class that describes and processes form fields.

Example:

python
from django import forms

class StudentForm(forms.Form):

    name = forms.CharField()

    age = forms.IntegerField()

    email = forms.EmailField()

This class describes a form containing:

text
name
age
email

3. Where Do We Put Forms?

Django apps commonly have:

text
students/
├── views.py
├── models.py
├── forms.py
├── urls.py
└── ...

Django doesn't necessarily create forms.py automatically with startapp.

You can create it yourself.

4. Creating forms.py

Inside your app:

text
students/forms.py

Write:

python
from django import forms

Then:

python
class StudentForm(forms.Form):

    name = forms.CharField()

    age = forms.IntegerField()

    email = forms.EmailField()

5. Understanding forms.Form

This:

python
class StudentForm(forms.Form):

means:

Create a Django form named StudentForm.

It inherits from:

python
forms.Form

Django then provides the form-processing functionality.

6. CharField

For text:

python
name = forms.CharField()

Example:

python
class StudentForm(forms.Form):

    name = forms.CharField()

This corresponds conceptually to a text input.

7. IntegerField

For integer values:

python
age = forms.IntegerField()

Django can validate that the submitted value can be interpreted as an integer.

8. EmailField

For email:

python
email = forms.EmailField()

Django provides email-format validation.

For example:

text
aman@example.com

is structurally email-like.

Whereas:

text
hello

would normally fail the field's email validation.

9. Complete Form

python
from django import forms


class StudentForm(forms.Form):

    name = forms.CharField()

    age = forms.IntegerField()

    email = forms.EmailField()

This is enough for Django to know that your form has three fields.

10. Rendering the Form

Now let's display it in a template.

View:

python
from django.shortcuts import render
from .forms import StudentForm


def student_form(request):

    form = StudentForm()

    return render(
        request,
        "student_form.html",
        {"form": form}
    )

Template:

html
<form method="POST">

    {% csrf_token %}

    {{ form }}

    <button type="submit">
        Submit
    </button>

</form>

Django generates HTML for the form fields.

11. What Does {{ form }} Do?

When you write:

html
{{ form }}

Django renders the form's fields as HTML.

Conceptually, it produces fields corresponding to:

text
Name
Age
Email

You don't have to manually create every <input>.

12. {{ form.as_p }}

A common rendering method is:

html
{{ form.as_p }}

It renders each field wrapped in a paragraph structure.

Example conceptually:

html
<p>
    <label>Name:</label>
    <input ...>
</p>

<p>
    <label>Age:</label>
    <input ...>
</p>

13. {{ form.as_table }}

You can write:

html
{{ form.as_table }}

This renders the form as table rows.

Typically you'd place it inside:

html
<table>
    {{ form.as_table }}
</table>

14. {{ form.as_ul }}

Another rendering option:

html
{{ form.as_ul }}

It renders the fields as list items.

Typically:

html
<ul>
    {{ form.as_ul }}
</ul>

15. Comparison

Syntax Typical output structure
{{ form }} Default form rendering
{{ form.as_p }} Paragraphs
{{ form.as_table }} Table rows
{{ form.as_ul }} List items

For exams, know all four.

16. Important: Rendering Is Not Validation

This is very important.

Creating:

python
form = StudentForm()

only creates a form instance.

It doesn't mean submitted data is valid.

For submitted data:

python
form = StudentForm(request.POST)

then:

python
form.is_valid()

performs validation.

17. Unbound vs Bound Form

This terminology is important.

Unbound form

python
form = StudentForm()

It has no submitted data.

Used when initially displaying the form.

Bound form

python
form = StudentForm(request.POST)

It contains submitted data and can be validated.

18. Visualizing This

text
StudentForm()
     ↓
Unbound form
     ↓
Display form

After submission:

text
request.POST
     ↓
StudentForm(request.POST)
     ↓
Bound form
     ↓
is_valid()
     ↓
Validation

This distinction is very important for viva.

19. is_valid()

The most important Django Forms method:

python
form.is_valid()

It validates the submitted data.

Example:

python
if form.is_valid():
    print("Valid")
else:
    print("Invalid")

It returns:

text
True

or:

text
False

20. Complete GET + POST Form View

This is a pattern you should memorize.

python
from django.shortcuts import render
from .forms import StudentForm


def student_form(request):

    if request.method == "POST":

        form = StudentForm(request.POST)

        if form.is_valid():

            print("Form is valid")

    else:

        form = StudentForm()

    return render(
        request,
        "student_form.html",
        {"form": form}
    )

Let's understand it carefully.

21. First Visit — GET

When the user opens:

text
/student-form/

the browser sends:

text
GET

So:

python
if request.method == "POST":

is false.

Django executes:

python
form = StudentForm()

An empty/unbound form is displayed.

22. Submission — POST

User fills:

text
Name: Aman
Age: 21
Email: aman@example.com

and clicks Submit.

Browser sends:

text
POST

Django executes:

python
form = StudentForm(request.POST)

Now the form is bound to submitted data.

23. Validation

Then:

python
if form.is_valid():

Django validates:

text
name
age
email

If everything is valid:

text
True

Otherwise:

text
False

24. cleaned_data

If the form is valid:

python
form.cleaned_data

contains the cleaned/validated values.

Example:

python
if form.is_valid():

    name = form.cleaned_data["name"]
    age = form.cleaned_data["age"]
    email = form.cleaned_data["email"]

This is preferred over directly using:

python
request.POST.get("name")

after form validation.

25. Why cleaned_data?

Suppose:

python
age = forms.IntegerField()

The browser sends form data as strings.

After validation, Django can convert the valid value into the appropriate Python type.

So:

python
form.cleaned_data["age"]

can be an integer.

This is one of the major benefits of Django Forms.

26. Example

Form:

python
class StudentForm(forms.Form):

    name = forms.CharField()

    age = forms.IntegerField()

Submitted:

text
name = "Aman"
age = "21"

After:

python
form.is_valid()

you can access:

python
form.cleaned_data["name"]

and:

python
form.cleaned_data["age"]

The second value can be an integer rather than the original raw string.

27. Form Errors

Suppose the user enters:

text
Age = abc

but:

python
age = forms.IntegerField()

Validation fails.

Then:

python
form.is_valid()

returns:

text
False

and Django stores validation errors in the form.

28. Displaying Errors

If your template contains:

html
<form method="POST">

    {% csrf_token %}

    {{ form }}

    <button type="submit">
        Submit
    </button>

</form>

Django can render the associated field errors along with the form.

You can also access them explicitly.

29. form.errors

In Python:

python
form.errors

contains validation errors.

Example:

python
if not form.is_valid():

    print(form.errors)

Useful for debugging and understanding validation.

30. Required Fields

By default, many Django form fields are required.

Example:

python
name = forms.CharField()

If the user submits it empty, validation generally fails.

31. required=False

You can make a field optional:

python
phone = forms.CharField(
    required=False
)

Now the user can leave it blank.

32. label

You can customize the field label:

python
name = forms.CharField(
    label="Student Name"
)

Django can use:

text
Student Name

instead of deriving the default label from name.

33. initial

You can provide an initial/default displayed value:

python
name = forms.CharField(
    initial="Aman"
)

The form initially displays:

text
Aman

The user can modify it unless other restrictions apply.

34. help_text

You can provide additional information:

python
name = forms.CharField(
    help_text="Enter your full name"
)

This can help explain what the field expects.

35. max_length

For text:

python
name = forms.CharField(
    max_length=100
)

This limits the accepted string length during form validation and can influence the generated HTML widget.

36. min_length

You can also specify:

python
name = forms.CharField(
    min_length=3
)

The submitted value must satisfy the minimum length requirement.

37. IntegerField Options

Example:

python
age = forms.IntegerField(
    min_value=18,
    max_value=100
)

Now the form expects an integer within that range.

For example:

text
21 → valid
17 → invalid
101 → invalid

38. EmailField

Example:

python
email = forms.EmailField()

Django validates that the value has a valid email-like structure.

39. ChoiceField

For a fixed set of choices:

python
course = forms.ChoiceField(
    choices=[
        ("cse", "Computer Science"),
        ("it", "Information Technology"),
        ("ece", "Electronics")
    ]
)

The first element is the submitted value.

The second is the human-readable label.

40. Understanding Choices

python
("cse", "Computer Science")

means:

text
submitted value → cse
displayed label → Computer Science

This distinction is very important.

41. BooleanField

Example:

python
agree = forms.BooleanField()

This is useful for things such as:

text
I agree to the terms

You can customize whether it is required.

42. DateField

Example:

python
dob = forms.DateField()

Django can validate and convert the submitted date according to the field's configuration.

43. Multiple Fields

A realistic form:

python
from django import forms


class StudentForm(forms.Form):

    name = forms.CharField(
        max_length=100
    )

    age = forms.IntegerField(
        min_value=16,
        max_value=100
    )

    email = forms.EmailField()

    course = forms.ChoiceField(
        choices=[
            ("cse", "Computer Science"),
            ("it", "Information Technology"),
        ]
    )

    dob = forms.DateField()

44. Complete Template

html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>

<head>
    <title>Student Form</title>
</head>

<body>

    <h1>Student Registration</h1>

    <form method="POST">

        {% csrf_token %}

        {{ form.as_p }}

        <button type="submit">
            Submit
        </button>

    </form>

</body>

</html>

45. Complete View

python
from django.shortcuts import render
from .forms import StudentForm


def student_form(request):

    if request.method == "POST":

        form = StudentForm(request.POST)

        if form.is_valid():

            name = form.cleaned_data["name"]
            age = form.cleaned_data["age"]
            email = form.cleaned_data["email"]
            course = form.cleaned_data["course"]
            dob = form.cleaned_data["dob"]

            print(name)
            print(age)
            print(email)
            print(course)
            print(dob)

    else:

        form = StudentForm()

    return render(
        request,
        "student_form.html",
        {"form": form}
    )

46. Complete Flow

Memorize this:

text
                User opens page
                      ↓
                     GET
                      ↓
             StudentForm()
                      ↓
               Empty form
                      ↓
                  User fills
                      ↓
                    POST
                      ↓
          StudentForm(request.POST)
                      ↓
                 is_valid()
                /          \
              Yes           No
               ↓             ↓
        cleaned_data      form.errors
               ↓             ↓
          Process data    Show errors

This is the core Django Forms workflow.

47. Why Use forms.Form Instead of Manual HTML?

Manual approach:

text
HTML fields
    ↓
request.POST
    ↓
manual validation
    ↓
manual conversion
    ↓
manual errors

Django Form:

text
Form class
    ↓
request.POST
    ↓
is_valid()
    ↓
cleaned_data
    ↓
errors

Much cleaner.

48. Form Field vs Model Field

This distinction becomes extremely important later.

Form field:

python
forms.CharField()

Used for:

User input and validation.

Model field:

python
models.CharField(max_length=100)

Used for:

Defining database structure.

We'll study ModelForms later when we reach Models.

49. Form vs ModelForm

You will eventually encounter:

python
forms.Form

and:

python
forms.ModelForm

Form

You manually define form fields.

python
class StudentForm(forms.Form):
    name = forms.CharField()

ModelForm

Django can generate form fields based on a model.

python
class StudentForm(forms.ModelForm):
    class Meta:
        model = Student
        fields = "__all__"

We'll study this later.

50. Common Mistake — Forgetting request.POST

Wrong:

python
form = StudentForm()

when processing submitted data.

Correct:

python
form = StudentForm(request.POST)

Otherwise Django doesn't have the submitted data to validate.

51. Common Mistake — Calling cleaned_data Before Validation

Wrong:

python
form = StudentForm(request.POST)

name = form.cleaned_data["name"]

Correct:

python
form = StudentForm(request.POST)

if form.is_valid():

    name = form.cleaned_data["name"]

cleaned_data should be used after successful validation.

52. Common Mistake — Forgetting CSRF

For a POST form:

html
<form method="POST">

    {% csrf_token %}

    {{ form.as_p }}

</form>

We'll study CSRF in detail in Module 23.

53. Common Mistake — Not Returning the Form

Suppose validation fails.

You generally want to render the bound form again:

python
return render(
    request,
    "student_form.html",
    {"form": form}
)

This allows Django to display validation errors and submitted values appropriately.

54. Viva Questions

Q1. What is a Django Form?

A Django Form is a Python class used to define, render, validate, and process user input.

Q2. Which module provides Django Forms?

python
from django import forms

Q3. What is forms.Form?

It is the base class used to create standard Django forms.

Q4. What is forms.CharField?

A form field designed primarily for text input and validation.

Q5. What is forms.IntegerField?

A form field that validates and converts integer input.

55. Viva — Bound vs Unbound

Teacher:

What is an unbound form?

Answer:

A form created without submitted data, such as StudentForm(), generally used to initially display an empty form.

Teacher:

What is a bound form?

Answer:

A form created with submitted data, such as StudentForm(request.POST), which can then be validated.

56. Viva — is_valid()

Teacher:

What does is_valid() do?

Answer:

It runs the form's validation process and returns True if the submitted data is valid and False otherwise.

57. Viva — cleaned_data

Teacher:

What is cleaned_data?

Answer:

cleaned_data is a dictionary containing the cleaned and validated form values after successful validation.

58. Viva — Why Not request.POST?

Teacher:

Why use cleaned_data instead of directly processing request.POST after validation?

Answer:

cleaned_data contains values after Django has performed the form field's validation and appropriate conversion, making it safer and easier to work with.

59. Viva — forms.Form vs ModelForm

Answer:

forms.Form requires fields to be explicitly defined, while forms.ModelForm can generate form fields from a Django model and is commonly used when a form corresponds to database data.

Create a form with:

  • name
  • age
  • email

class StudentForm(forms.Form):

    name = forms.CharField()

    age = forms.IntegerField()

    email = forms.EmailField()

Write a view that displays the form on GET and validates it on POST.

from django.shortcuts import render
from .forms import StudentForm


def student_form(request):

    if request.method == "POST":

        form = StudentForm(request.POST)

        if form.is_valid():

            name = form.cleaned_data["name"]

            print(name)

    else:

If your teacher asks:
